fields.meta_description: Build a file upload form from a prompt. Set accepted file types and a size cap, take photos on a phone, and keep each file with its submission.
fields.h1: Build a File Upload Form That Sorts Every File on Arrival
fields.hero_description: Describe the files people need to send. Emergent builds the file upload form with type and size checks and saves each file with its submission, in storage you own.
fields.features_heading: What a File Field Needs Behind It
fields.features_subheading: An upload button takes a minute to add. These six pieces decide whether each file reaches the right person and the right record.
fields.feature_1:
Only the file types you can open

Choose the formats each field accepts, like PDF for a signed contract. Anything else is stopped at the field with a plain message, while the person is still on the page to fix it.
fields.feature_2:
A size cap people see up front

Set the largest file each field takes and show it in the help text. A file over the cap is turned away with its own size beside the limit, and every other answer stays filled in.
fields.feature_3:
Photos straight from the phone camera

On a phone, the upload field offers the camera next to the photo library. People photograph a receipt or a damaged part and send it with no file to save and no account to sign in to.
fields.feature_4:
Each file stays with its submission

Files are saved to storage you own and linked to the row they arrived with. Open an order or a claim and the attachments sit right there, instead of in a folder of loose downloads.
fields.feature_5:
File names you can sort, on arrival

Rename each file as it lands, using answers from the form such as the order number or a last name. IMG_4471.jpg becomes 10482-proof.jpg, and a search by order number finds it.
fields.feature_6:
The upload form, in your GitHub repo

Export the form with its checks and storage rules to your own repository. A developer can change the accepted types or point uploads at a different bucket without rebuilding it.
fields.why_title: Why Build File Upload Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Most form tools can take a file. They differ on who has to sign in to send one and where the file ends up afterward.

fields.usecase_heading: What People Send Through an Upload Form
fields.tab_content_1:
Artwork arrives named after its order

Customers ordering menus from Kestrel Print upload artwork on the order form. The field takes PDF and PNG files up to 50 MB and refuses anything else before submit. A file called menu-final.pdf lands as 10482-menu-final.pdf, attached to order 10482 in the prepress queue.
fields.tab_content_2:
A photo of the cracked lamp travels with the return

A shopper whose lamp arrived cracked opens the Alder Home return form on her phone and takes the picture from inside the upload field. It is saved to her return for order 7731 with the reason she picked. Support sees the crack in the queue and approves a replacement without asking for photos.
fields.tab_content_3:
By day 3, any missing document triggers a reminder

Each borrower owes Northwind Lending four documents before underwriting, and the form shows which have arrived. When one is still missing after 3 days, the borrower gets an email that names it and links back to the same file. The loan officer's dashboard marks that loan as waiting until the upload comes in.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each project arrives named by student and module

Final projects for the Fieldnote design course come in as PDFs through one form. Every file is renamed with the student's last name and Module 4 before it reaches the instructor's board. The deadline is Friday at 5 p.m., and a project uploaded after that shows a Late tag with its upload time.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a File Upload Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what you expect to receive before you add a single field. The form gets simpler once that list exists.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the formats your team can open
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set a size cap for each field
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide which record a file belongs to
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each document or photo you need and what happens to it once it arrives. A print order needs one artwork file. A loan file might need several documents from one borrower, and each one deserves its own labeled field.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Accept only the formats someone on your side can use. PDF suits documents that will be printed or signed. iPhones capture photos in HEIF, saved as .heic files, unless the camera is set to Most Compatible, which saves JPEG instead.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Base each cap on the files you expect, such as 10 MB for a receipt photo and a larger limit for design files. Put the cap in the field's help text so nobody learns about it after waiting through a slow upload.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tie each upload to the thing it proves, like an order number or a claim. Pick a naming rule built from form answers, and decide who gets an alert when a file arrives. Those choices are what make a file findable later.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write a prompt that lists each field with its accepted formats and size cap, plus the naming rule. Emergent builds the form and the table that links every upload to its submission. Change any part of it later by asking.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Plan for files that come later
fields.howto_step_6_des: Some people can answer today but need a week to find a document. Decide whether the upload is required to submit. If it can wait, send an emailed link that reopens the same submission for the late file.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the form from a phone on mobile data. Try a photo taken on the spot, a file in the wrong format, and one over the cap. Then confirm the error text reads clearly and the stored file opens with the expected name.

plan.angle: The top 10 is plugin templates (Elfsight, Static Forms), how-to videos and articles for Microsoft Forms, Google Forms and WordPress, and a Google forum thread about a missing upload option. All of them stop once the file field exists. This page starts there: which file types and sizes a form should accept, how a phone photo gets in, where each file lands and how it stays tied to the right order, claim or person, and what happens when a required document never arrives. Four real collection jobs carry it: print artwork, a damage claim photo, a loan document checklist and course project hand-ins.
